   - `%e` = executable filename
   - `%p` = process ID
   - `%t` = timestamp
   - Core dumps will be saved to `/tmp/` with this naming scheme

2. **`ulimit -c unlimited`**
   - Removes the limit on core dump file size
   - Allows core dumps of any size to be generated

**To run these commands yourself:**

```bash

ulimit -c unlimited
```

**Note:** 
- The first command requires `sudo` (root privileges) since it modifies a kernel parameter
- The second command only affects the current shell session
- To make `ulimit -c unlimited` persistent, add it to your shell configuration file (`.bashrc`, `.zshrc`, etc.)
